newsitem.title: UK: FTSE seen cautiously firmer, awaits rate decision.
newsitem.headline: FTSE seen cautiously firmer, awaits rate decision.

text.p: ** FTSE 100 expected to open 15-20 points higher after Dow
ends more than 100 points ahead, having stood sharply
** Market awaits possible UK rate hike as two-day monetary
meeting starts and following Tuesday's inflation figures.
The FTSE 100 is expected to open 15-20 points higher, cheered by a huge rise for the Dow overnight, dealers said.
The U.S. index rose 103.82 points to 7,962.31, having traded sharply lower at the London close. The FTSE 100 ended more than 50 points weaker.
"We may see the FTSE 100 up at the very beginning as a knee-jerk reaction to Wall Street but the broader market will be easier. Everyone's concentrating on the monetary meeting today," said a dealer.

Today sees the start of a two-day monetary policy meeting to debate a possible rise in interest rates. The decision is expected tomorrow and is seen bringing a rise of a quarter to half a point in interest rates from the current 6.5 percent.
Business is seen subdued as the market awaits the Bank of England's decision and FTSE 100 prices are expected to ease after an initial mark-up.

"We're not going to see many people wanting to buy on a day like today, with that sort of thing hanging in the balance and although they'll probably try to push the market higher we won't see that lasting," said another dealer.
Tuesday's inflation figures showing a rise to 2.9 percent in June from an annual 2.6 percent are seen forcing the Bank's hand on interest rates.

The FTSE 100 is still being driven by technical factors and continues to track index futures closely, while the broader market reflects worries over interest rate moves and the strength of sterling, dealers said.

"There's a two-tier market at the moment, with the FTSE 100 squeezed in places depending on what the books are like across the tracks and the FTSE 250 and FTSE 350 showing more of what market sentiment really is," he said.
There is no scheduled economic news today to alter the market's focus on tomorrow's decision.
Major scheduled company news is also scarce today.
Dixons is seen rising after full year figures and a bullish current trading statement.
